newsitem.title: UK: UK January gas output sets new record - WoodMac.
newsitem.headline: UK January gas output sets new record - WoodMac.

text.p: The average rate of natural gas produced in January in the U.K. set a new record at 12,330 million cubic feet a day (mmcfd), consultants Wood Mackenzie said on Tuesday in their March North Sea Report.
This is up by 256 mmcfd from the previous record of 12,074 mmcfd, set in February 1996. Output in January was also up by 8 percent from the corresponding total in January 1996.

The Morecambe fields, now part of Centrica plc, the supply arm of the demerged British Gas plc, contributed around 12 percent of the total, at 1,445 mmcfd, even though this was a fall of 229 mmcfd from December's level of 1,674 mmcfd.
The Brent field also produced a record volume of 637 mmcfd, over 5 percent of total UK production and up from 556 mmcfd in January, Wood Mackenzie said.
Strong demand was shown by the drawdown in supplies held in the Rough storage facility, it said.

Rough produced a "positive net effect," when gas is produced from the reservoir, of 392 mmcfd. During January the high level of demand was also shown by a series of interruptions to interruptible customers at the beginning of the month.

Production fell at Hamilton North, by 16 mmcfd, as Hamilton came onstream at the end of the month, it said. Nelson also saw a fall, by 13 mmcfd, as a gas cooler failed and gas exports were stopped for two weeks for repairs.

Gas deliveries through the Bacton terminal were dropped by 18 mmcfd on the same period the previous year, as Amoco experienced problems with its Inde 23a production complex. This feeds gas fom the Indefatigable, Davy, Bessemer and Beaufort fields into Bacton.

Throughput was interrupted to allow repairs to a weakened weld, and the repairs were done between January 1 to 3, putting further pressure on supplies during the period of peak demand, Wood Mackenzie said.
